jobs.description:
Position Overview And Responsibilities

The Srinivasan Laboratory at Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation (OMRF) is recruiting a motivated Research Technician to study the development and disease mechanisms of lymphatic vessels and cardiovascular valves.

Our research addresses diseases including lymphedema, aortic stenosis, mitral valve prolapse, venous valve dysfunction, thrombosis, and inflammatory disorders. We use multidisciplinary approaches including genetically engineered mouse models, advanced imaging, molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, and bioinformatics.

Successful candidates will have opportunities to develop independent research directions, learn new experimental and computational approaches, present their work at scientific meetings, and contribute to high-impact publications.

Selected Publications

Cha et al., Genes & Development (2016)
Geng et al., JCI Insight (2020)
Chen et al., Development (2020)
Ho et al., Circulation Research (2023)
Geng et al., Journal of Experimental Medicine (2025)

More information: https://srinivasan.omrf.org/

How To Apply

In addition to applying online, please send the following to Sathish Srinivasan, Ph.D. at Sathish-Srinivasan@omrf.org:

CV
Brief description of research experience, interests, and career goals
Contact information for three references

Candidate Profile

Relevant backgrounds include Cell Biology, Developmental Biology, Vascular Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Genetics, Immunology, or Bioinformatics. Experience with mouse models, imaging, genomics, or computational analysis is desirable but not required.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a biological science or related field, or an equivalent combination of relevant laboratory experience.
Ability and willingness to handle laboratory mice, including breeding, maintenance, and procedures as needed.
Basic proficiency with computers, including internet browsing, order processing systems, and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Ability to comprehend instructions, follow protocols, and perform precise, accurate work when handling samples and chemicals.
Strong analytical skills, including the ability to compute basic mathematical operations such as rates, ratios, percentages, molarity, and unit conversions.
Excellent oral and written communication skills for documenting procedures, summarizing data, and collaborating effectively with team members.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience working with laboratory mice, PCR genotyping, histology, microscopy and molecular biology techniques are highly desirable.

Work Hours

Work hours are typically Monday – Friday, 8:30am – 5pm.

OMRF Overview

Founded in 1946, the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation (OMRF) is among the nation’s oldest, most respected independent, nonprofit biomedical research institutes. OMRF is dedicated to understanding and developing more effective treatments for human diseases, focusing on critical research areas such as Alzheimer’s disease, cancer, lupus, multiple sclerosis, and cardiovascular disease. OMRF follows an innovative cross-disciplinary approach to medical research and ranks among the nation’s leaders in patents per scientist.

Located in Oklahoma City, a city that offers a dynamic and flourishing downtown area, with low cost of living, short commute times and a diversified economy, OMRF has been voted one of the Top Workplaces since the inception of the award. This achievement has been accomplished thanks to OMRF individuals who share a unified understanding that our excellence can only be fully realized with a collective commitment to our mission, “. . . so that more may live longer, healthier lives.” Successful candidates will demonstrate commitment to this mission.

OMRF Benefits

We offer competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits to full-time employees including medical, dental, and vision insurance, minimum 8% company retirement contribution, vacation and sick leave, and paid holidays. All employees have access to our onsite café, free onsite fitness center with access to personal trainer, free parking and much more! Relocation assistance available for those located 50 miles outside of Oklahoma City metro. Learn more about our benefits here.

jobs.title: Research Assistant – X-ray Crystallography & Crystal Harvesting
jobs.description:
RiboForge | Los Angeles, California | On-Site | Full-Time

About RiboForge

RiboForge is a stealth biotechnology company based in Los Angeles. We are building a team with deep expertise in structural biology and X-ray crystallography and are seeking motivated researchers to support our experimental work.

About the Role

We are seeking a Research Assistant whose primary focus will be hands-on crystal harvesting and preparation of samples for X-ray diffraction studies
.

Most of your bench work will center on identifying and fishing crystals under a microscope, mounting them in loops, performing cryoprotection and flash-freezing, and maintaining organized cryogenic sample storage. Your work will directly support the quality and throughput of RiboForge’s crystallographic screening efforts.

This role is well suited to someone who enjoys precise microscope work, handles delicate samples carefully, and maintains consistency across repeated harvesting sessions. You will work closely with our scientists to improve harvesting workflows and prepare crystals for diffraction experiments.

Key Responsibilities

Harvest crystals:
Identify, select, and fish protein or nucleic acid crystals from crystallization drops under a microscope using appropriate loops and mounting tools.
Prepare crystals for diffraction:
Carry out cryoprotection, mounting, flash-freezing, and cryogenic storage according to established protocols.
Maintain sample traceability:
Accurately label and track harvested crystals, recording crystallization conditions, sample identities, storage locations, and handling observations.
Improve harvesting consistency:
Work with scientists to troubleshoot crystal damage, sample loss, and variability during harvesting and freezing.
Support crystallization experiments:
Set up crystallization screens, monitor crystal growth, and assist with optimization of conditions.
Prepare reagents and samples:
Make buffers, stock solutions, and cryoprotectants using accurate micropipetting and appropriate sample-handling techniques.
Document and communicate results:
Maintain complete experimental records and coordinate sample preparation with the team’s diffraction schedules.

Required Qualifications

Hands-on experience harvesting protein or nucleic acid crystals for X-ray crystallography, including fishing crystals under a microscope, mounting, and freezing.
Careful technique when manipulating small, fragile crystals and working with small sample volumes.
Patience and sustained attention to detail during repeated microscope-based tasks.
Basic wet lab proficiency, including micropipetting and preparation of buffers, stock solutions, and dilutions.
Strong organizational skills and a consistent approach to sample labeling, tracking, and experimental documentation.
Clear communication and the ability to follow protocols, recognize problems, and work collaboratively to resolve them.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience handling protein or nucleic acid crystals and using appropriate techniques to preserve sample integrity.
Familiarity with crystallization screening, optimization, and cryoprotectant selection.
Experience preparing cryogenic sample inventories or organizing samples for synchrotron diffraction experiments.
A bachelor’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, chemistry, or a related field is a plus, but is not required.

Experience harvesting protein crystals is relevant and welcome; prior RNA crystallography experience is a plus.

Compensation and Benefits

Anticipated full-time compensation is $70,000 per year, with flexibility to increase based on experience and qualifications. Part-time compensation and benefits eligibility will be discussed based on the position and schedule. Health coverage and benefits are included for full-time positions. Relocation assistance may be considered based on the candidate’s qualifications and circumstances.

How to Apply

Submit your resume, cover letter, and references to careers@riboforge.com
with the subject line “Research Assistant – X-ray Crystallography & Crystal Harvesting.”

In your application email, include two to three sentences describing your hands-on experience with crystal harvesting
, including the types of crystals you have worked with and your experience fishing, mounting, and freezing them.

Please also indicate whether you are interested in a part-time position, full-time position, or either
, along with your availability.

RiboForge | Los Angeles, California | On-Site | Full-Time

About RiboForge

RiboForge is a stealth biotechnology company based in Los Angeles. We are building a team with deep expertise in structural biology and X-ray crystallography and are seeking motivated researchers to support our experimental work.

About the Role

We are seeking a Research Assistant whose primary focus will be hands-on crystal harvesting and preparation of samples for X-ray diffraction studies
.

Most of your bench work will center on identifying and fishing crystals under a microscope, mounting them in loops, performing cryoprotection and flash-freezing, and maintaining organized cryogenic sample storage. Your work will directly support the quality and throughput of RiboForge’s crystallographic screening efforts.

This role is well suited to someone who enjoys precise microscope work, handles delicate samples carefully, and maintains consistency across repeated harvesting sessions. You will work closely with our scientists to improve harvesting workflows and prepare crystals for diffraction experiments.

Key Responsibilities

Harvest crystals:
Identify, select, and fish protein or nucleic acid crystals from crystallization drops under a microscope using appropriate loops and mounting tools.
Prepare crystals for diffraction:
Carry out cryoprotection, mounting, flash-freezing, and cryogenic storage according to established protocols.
Maintain sample traceability:
Accurately label and track harvested crystals, recording crystallization conditions, sample identities, storage locations, and handling observations.
Improve harvesting consistency:
Work with scientists to troubleshoot crystal damage, sample loss, and variability during harvesting and freezing.
Support crystallization experiments:
Set up crystallization screens, monitor crystal growth, and assist with optimization of conditions.
Prepare reagents and samples:
Make buffers, stock solutions, and cryoprotectants using accurate micropipetting and appropriate sample-handling techniques.
Document and communicate results:
Maintain complete experimental records and coordinate sample preparation with the team’s diffraction schedules.

Required Qualifications

Hands-on experience harvesting protein or nucleic acid crystals for X-ray crystallography, including fishing crystals under a microscope, mounting, and freezing.
Careful technique when manipulating small, fragile crystals and working with small sample volumes.
Patience and sustained attention to detail during repeated microscope-based tasks.
Basic wet lab proficiency, including micropipetting and preparation of buffers, stock solutions, and dilutions.
Strong organizational skills and a consistent approach to sample labeling, tracking, and experimental documentation.
Clear communication and the ability to follow protocols, recognize problems, and work collaboratively to resolve them.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience handling protein or nucleic acid crystals and using appropriate techniques to preserve sample integrity.
Familiarity with crystallization screening, optimization, and cryoprotectant selection.
Experience preparing cryogenic sample inventories or organizing samples for synchrotron diffraction experiments.
A bachelor’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, chemistry, or a related field is a plus, but is not required.

Experience harvesting protein crystals is relevant and welcome; prior RNA crystallography experience is a plus.

Compensation and Benefits

Anticipated full-time compensation is $70,000 per year, with flexibility to increase based on experience and qualifications. Part-time compensation and benefits eligibility will be discussed based on the position and schedule. Health coverage and benefits are included for full-time positions. Relocation assistance may be considered based on the candidate’s qualifications and circumstances.

How to Apply

Submit your resume, cover letter, and references to careers@riboforge.com
with the subject line “Research Assistant – X-ray Crystallography & Crystal Harvesting.”

In your application email, include two to three sentences describing your hands-on experience with crystal harvesting
, including the types of crystals you have worked with and your experience fishing, mounting, and freezing them.

Please also indicate whether you are interested in a part-time position, full-time position, or either
, along with your availability.
